newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraqi paper attacks U.N. human rights envoy.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi paper attacks U.N. human rights envoy.

text.p: The Iraqi government newspaper al-Jumhouriya on Monday branded the U.N. special investigator for human rights in Iraq a racist and a "human beast".

"One of outstanding human beasts is Max van der Stoel...This racist is used to utter lies against Iraq from time to time in order to distort its image and prolong the embargo on the Iraqi people," Jumhouriya said in a front-page editorial.

Van der Stoel, a former Dutch foreign minister who serves as U.N. Human Rights Commission's special rapporteur on Iraq, said in his annual report to the commission last week that there had been no improvement in human rights situation in Iraq over the last year.
Jumhouriya said van der Stoel was one of the "mercenaries who lost their human consciousness and turned to beasts which are trained on committing harm whenever they are ordered by Washington".
Van der Stoel also called on Baghdad to clear up the fate of 607 Kuwaitis and other nationals missing since the 1991 Gulf War over Kuwait.
Jumhouriya said on Monday an Iraqi group planned to publicise the pictures of missing Kuwaitis.
Iraq said it has freed all those captured but has promised to look at the issue again.
